books.title: 48 Laws of Power
books.author: Robert Greene
books.thesis: Power operates by hidden rules that reverse common moral instincts; understanding them is essential to survival.
books.topApplication: Question whose interests are actually served in any situation; assume strategic intent even in everyday interactions.

books.title: Laws of Human Nature
books.author: Robert Greene
books.thesis: Human nature follows predictable laws rooted in evolutionary psychology and social hierarchy; mastering them lets you navigate people and yourself.
books.topApplication: Identify which psychological law is operating in a conflict and respond to the underlying motive, not the surface complaint.

books.title: The Secret History of the World
books.author: Jonathan Black
books.thesis: Hidden esoteric and occult movements shaped world events more than official histories reveal; understanding these currents explains cultural shifts.
books.topApplication: Look beneath surface narratives in history and culture; follow the networks of influence that shaped decisions.

books.title: Nonviolent Communication
books.author: Marshall Rosenberg
books.thesis: Conflict arises from unmet needs; framing communication around needs, not judgments, transforms both the other person and yourself.
books.topApplication: When a conversation turns adversarial, pause and identify the underlying need (yours and theirs) before responding.

books.title: Becoming Supernatural
books.author: Joe Dispenza
books.thesis: Consciousness and belief literally reshape biology and reality; meditation and focused intention rewire your brain and nervous system.
books.topApplication: Use breathwork and visualization to interrupt anxiety patterns and rehearse new emotional responses before they're tested in real situations.

books.title: Fight Right
books.author: Harriet Lerner
books.thesis: Productive conflict requires skills: staying calm, listening, taking responsibility, and repairing afterward; most people never learn them.
books.topApplication: Before entering a difficult conversation, set an intention to stay curious about the other person's perspective, not to win.

books.title: God
books.author: Reza Aslan
books.thesis: The human concept of God has evolved across cultures and centuries; understanding this history reveals more about human nature than theology.
books.topApplication: Examine which of your beliefs about ultimate meaning come from your culture's narrative versus your own direct experience.

books.title: The Infinite Game
books.author: Simon Sinek
books.thesis: Business and life are infinite games with no finish line; success comes from choosing worthy rivals, building trust, and playing to continue.
books.topApplication: Identify whether you're playing to win (finite mindset) or to keep playing (infinite mindset) — then shift if it doesn't serve your goals.

books.title: Hunt Gather Parent
books.author: Michaeleen Doucleff
books.thesis: Global parenting practices reveal that kids thrive on autonomy, clear boundaries, and meaningful responsibility — not intensive oversight.
books.topApplication: Let your kids struggle with age-appropriate challenges; your job is boundaries, not rescue.

books.title: The New Psycho-Cybernetics
books.author: Maxwell Maltz
books.thesis: Your self-image is a servo-mechanism; change it, and your behavior and outcomes follow automatically.
books.topApplication: When stuck, ask 'What would someone who already has what I want do?' and visualize that version of yourself acting that way.

books.title: It's Not Always Depression
books.author: Hilary Jacobs Hendel
books.thesis: What looks like depression is often defensive numbing of other core emotions (anger, grief, fear); treating the defense doesn't fix the root.
books.topApplication: When you feel flat or unmotivated, pause and ask: what emotion am I avoiding? What would happen if I let myself feel it?

books.title: Cues
books.author: Vanessa Van Edwards
books.thesis: Your brain reads micro-signals in the environment to decide if you're safe or threatened; mastering these cues lets you influence how others read you.
books.topApplication: Before high-stakes meetings, control the room's cues: temperature, posture, background, lighting — signal calm, not chaos.

books.title: Sapiens
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.thesis: Human dominance rests on shared fictions (gods, nations, corporations); understanding this reveals both our power and our fragility.
books.topApplication: Recognize the 'stories' your company, family, or culture live by — question which ones serve you and which limit you.

books.title: The Old Man and the Sea
books.author: Ernest Hemingway
books.thesis: A man's worth comes from his struggle and dignity in defeat, not in winning; grace is found in enduring with honor.
books.topApplication: When facing a loss or setback, focus on how you carry yourself through it — that choice is always yours.

books.title: Man and His Symbols
books.author: Carl Jung
books.thesis: Symbols in dreams and myths reveal the universal patterns of the human psyche; understanding yours gives you access to your own depths.
books.topApplication: When a dream or story haunts you, spend time with what it symbolizes about your own inner world.

books.title: Coach Wooden's Pyramid of Success
books.author: John Wooden
books.thesis: Sustainable success (personal or team) is built on a foundation of fundamentals practiced obsessively, not shortcuts or talent alone.
books.topApplication: Pick one fundamental skill in your work or life and practice it daily at the level of a beginner until it becomes invisible.
